name: ETSI Open Source MANO (OSM)
what_it_is: OSM is an ETSI-hosted open source NFV Management and Orchestration stack (Apache 2.0) that implements the ETSI NFV MANO architecture. It orchestrates the lifecycle of Virtualised Network Functions (VNFs) and Network Services across heterogeneous cloud and container infrastructure.
components: NBI (North Bound Interface) — SOL005-aligned REST API consumed by OSS/BSS
RO (Resource Orchestrator) — allocates compute/network/storage across VIMs
LCM (Lifecycle Manager) — drives VNF/NS instantiation, scaling, healing, termination
MON (Monitoring module) — collects metrics from VNFs and VIMs, feeds autoscaling policies
POL (Policy module) — enforces autoscaling and healing rules
VCA (VNF Configuration and Abstraction) — Juju-based Day-1/Day-2 config primitives
OSM Client (osmclient) — Python CLI and library for remote API access
Keystone — OpenStack identity service used for multi-tenant RBAC
WIM (Wide-area Network Inter-VIM SDN) — optional SDN controller integration
Prometheus exporter — exposes OSM metrics for external scraping
protocols: SOL005 (Os-Ma-nfvo) — NBI API for NS lifecycle and VNF package management
SOL006 — YANG-based NSD/VNFD information model (OSM IM)
SOL002 / SOL003 — Ve-Vnfm interfaces for VNF lifecycle (via LCM)
Juju remote procedure calls — VCA communication with charms
Kafka — internal event bus between OSM microservices
gRPC — inter-service communication for some modules
OpenStack REST APIs (Nova, Neutron, Cinder, Glance, Heat)
Kubernetes API — for KNF (Kubernetes-based NF) orchestration
Helm v3 — packaging and deployment of KNFs on Kubernetes
measurement: MON module polls VIM telemetry (OpenStack Ceilometer/Gnocchi, Prometheus) and exposes aggregated metrics
Prometheus exporter endpoint on OSM for scraping orchestration-layer KPIs (NS count, VNF state, alarm counts)
Autoscaling decisions driven by threshold-based rules defined in the VNFD scaling policy
Audit log stream records all NBI API calls with timestamps and user identity for compliance measurement
configuration: Day-1 config delivered via Juju charms attached to VNF descriptors (VCA)
Day-2 config primitives (exec-env actions) invokable through NBI after instantiation
LDAP external authentication integration for enterprise identity providers
Role-Based Access Control (RBAC) with project/user scoping via Keystone
Helm values overrides for KNF parametrisation at instantiation time
OSM installed via single-script installer, Charmed OSM (Juju bundle), or Helm chart for Kubernetes-hosted control plane
fault_injection: No native fault-injection framework; OSM does not ship a chaos or fault-injection module
VDU rebuild and VDU migrate operations can simulate failure recovery workflows via NBI
Healing policies in POL module can be triggered manually to test self-healing paths
modes: HA cluster mode with distributed microservices across multiple nodes
Charmed OSM — Juju-bundle deployment for production-grade installs
Helm-based deployment — OSM control plane running inside Kubernetes
Development mode — lightweight environment for contributor testing
constraints: Release NINETEEN is the current stable version as of early 2026; older releases are unsupported and may lack SOL006 YANG model features
VCA (Juju) is a hard runtime dependency for Day-2 config primitives; environments without outbound Juju controller access lose Day-2 capability
OpenVIM and VMware vCloud Director VIM drivers are deprecated and may be removed in future releases
OSM does not natively implement SOL004 (VNF package format) validation tooling — external validators are required
Kubernetes KNF support requires Helm v3; Helm v2 deployments are unsupported
Multi-site WAN stitching via WIM requires a compatible SDN controller (e.g., ONOS, ODL); OSM does not include one
notable_absences: No built-in fault injection or chaos engineering tooling
No native SOL004 VNF package validator shipped with the platform
No SDN controller bundled — WIM integration requires an external controller
No built-in CI/CD pipeline for onboarding VNF packages; relies on external tooling
No GUI-based network topology editor for composing Network Service Descriptors
